channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Conselho de Ética julga representações contra Pollon por participar de motim e xingar Motta
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Ethics Council is ruling this Tuesday (14) on two complaints against Deputy Marcos Pollon (PL-MS) for conduct incompatible with parliamentary decorum: obstructing proceedings during the August 2025 riot, when he was the last to retreat after Bolsonaro's arrest, and insulting Chamber President Hugo Motta, calling him a 'bosta' and 'baixinho' in a speech in Mato Grosso do Sul. The suspension requests range from 30 to 90 days, both cases linked to the bolsonarist reaction to Bolsonaro's STF conviction for attempted coup.

item.title: Jorge Seif pede asilo político nos EUA para Ramagem
item.description: Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC) submitted a political asylum request to the U.S. Embassy on behalf of former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL), detained in Orlando by ICE, claiming political persecution over his STF convictions for attempted coup and criminal organization. Seif contends the evidence is weak, cites Justice Luiz Fux’s dissenting vote, and criticizes Justice Alexandre de Moraes, sanctioned by OFAC for alleged human rights abuses.

item.title: Zema diz que Moraes e Toffoli “merecem prisão” e defende impeachment no STF
item.description: Presidential pré-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) stated that Supreme Court ministers Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli 'deserve imprisonment' and advocated for their impeachment, calling the situation a 'moral crisis' and criticizing the 'impunity of the untouchables' in Brasília. He also linked high interest rates to federal government 'spending spree,' claiming it harms families and businesses, and affirmed his intention to continue his pré-campaign until the end as a political alternative.

item.title: Senador bolsonarista apela ao governo americano para conceder asilo a Ramagem
item.description: Bolsonarist Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC) appealed to the U.S. Embassy in Brazil to grant political asylum to Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency (Abin), who was arrested by ICE in Florida after fleeing the country in September 2023. Seif claims Ramagem is a victim of political persecution by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, citing alleged human rights violations, despite the U.S. having lifted sanctions against Moraes in December. Ramagem was sentenced to over 16 years for his role in the January 8 coup plot and lost his congressional mandate.

item.title: Lula indica Pimenta como novo líder do Governo na Câmara
item.description: President Lula appointed Deputy Paulo Pimenta as the new Government Leader in the Chamber of Deputies, replacing José Guimarães, who moved to head the Secretariat of Institutional Relations. Guimarães, in turn, replaces Gleisi Hoffmann in the government’s political coordination, as she prepares to run for Senate in 2026. The reshuffle aims to strengthen congressional coordination, particularly with the Centrist bloc, amid legislative challenges including presidential vetoes and priority bills.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara transforma sabatina em discurso e evita perguntas a candidatos ao TCU
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee decided to replace the traditional confirmation hearing for TCU ministerial candidates with 10-minute speeches, avoiding any question-and-answer session. The agreement, made to skip the scheduled hearing on April 13, 2026, favors unilateral presentations by the seven party-nominated candidates over substantive scrutiny.

item.title: O recado de Cármen Lúcia sobre a crise de imagem no Supremo Tribunal Federal
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia acknowledged a crisis of trust and image in the Supreme Federal Court, attributing it to the law's inability to keep pace with technological and social changes such as AI, social media, and debates on free speech, the environment, climate, and indigenous rights. She noted that 49% of Brazilians distrust the STF and advocated for greater transparency and discussion of reforms to address the credibility crisis, stating the current functioning cannot remain unchanged.

item.title: Preso pela polícia migratória de Trump, Ramagem comemorou volta do republicano ao poder em 2024
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem, ex-head of Brazil's intelligence agency (Abin) and sentenced to 16 years for involvement in the coup plot, was arrested in Orlando, Florida, by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after fleeing Brazil in September 2025. He had celebrated Donald Trump's 2024 victory on X (formerly Twitter), linking the Republican's return to power with hopes for political change in Brazil, including Jair Bolsonaro's potential return in 2026.

item.title: Cotado para a vice de Flávio, Zema cita direita 'envovlida com coisas erradas' e critica 'frutas podres' no PL
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema criticized the right for being involved in 'wrongdoings' and said the PL has 'rotten fruits', amid speculation he could be Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate in 2026. Zema also called for the imprisonment of STF ministers Dias Toffoli and Alexandre de Moraes, reaffirming his own presidential candidacy despite rumors of a vice-presidential role.

item.title: Empréstimo para túnel Santos-Guarujá vira nova frente de disputa de paternidade entre Lula e Tarcísio
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin participated in the signing of a R$ 2.6 billion loan by Banco do Brasil to the São Paulo state government, led by Tarcísio de Freitas, to fund the state’s contribution to the Santos-Guarujá tunnel project. Although the loan was made to the state government, it sparked a political dispute over credit for the initiative between the federal Lula administration and the state Tarcísio administration, as both seek to associate themselves with this strategic infrastructure project.

item.title: Lula anuncia Paulo Pimenta como novo líder do governo na Câmara
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced Deputy Paulo Pimenta as the new government leader in the Chamber of Deputados, replacing José Guimarães, who will assume the Secretariat of Institutional Relations. Pimenta, a former Minister of Communications and experienced PT leader with prior roles in congressional committees, returns to the government leadership post. Guimarães will be sworn in as SRI minister on Tuesday (14) following Hoffmann’s departure due to electoral incompatibility rules.

item.title: “Moraes e Toffoli não merecem impeachment, merecem prisão”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor and pre-candidate for President from Novo, said STF ministers Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli deserve imprisonment, not impeachment, over alleged ties to Banco Master. He called them 'untouchable' and said the climate of outrage for the 2026 elections is greater than in 2018.

item.title: Nova lei torna vacina contra o câncer prioridade no Sistema Único de Saúde
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.385/26, which prioritizes access to cancer vaccines, medications, and advanced therapies through the SUS. The law establishes the National Policy for Cancer Prevention and Control, emphasizing individualized treatments based on tumor genetic analysis, and promotes domestic innovation via FNDCT funding and support for biotech startups.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira diz que Eduardo Bolsonaro atrapalha direita
item.description: PP national leader Ciro Nogueira said Eduardo Bolsonaro hinders the right by fueling internal disputes that distract from opposing President Lula’s government. He argued that the real adversary is not figures like Eduardo or Nikolas Ferreira, but the need to unite the right around core issues such as security, health, education, and competitiveness. The remarks were made at the HBR Summit Brazil 2026, as the PP discusses a strategic alliance with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula vence apenas se transformar eleição em plebiscito sobre soberania nacional
item.description: Lula faces a serious risk of not being re-elected due to high rejection rates, while Flávio Bolsonaro, running in his father’s name, represents a threat of reactionarism and submission to Trump’s interests. The text argues that the 2026 election must be framed as a plebiscite on national sovereignty, asserting that only the current government led by Lula and Alckmin can preserve Brazil’s independence amid external pressures from deglobalization.

item.title: TSE pode cassar o governador de Roraima e tornar Denarium inelegível nesta terça
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) resumes this Tuesday the trial that could remove the governor of Roraima, Edilson Damião (União), from office and render former governor Antonio Denarium (Republicanos) ineligible, who resigned in March to run for Senate. Two judges have already voted for conviction over allegations of irregular distribution of basic food baskets during the electoral campaign, using social programs like 'Cesta da Família' and 'Morar Melhor'. A majority requires two more justices to follow the rapporteur, Minister Isabel Gallotti.

item.title: Após avanço no Datafolha, Flávio Bolsonaro reforça ofensiva em eleitorado feminino e no Nordeste
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is technically tied with Lula in the second round according to a Datafolha poll, with 46% to 45%. His campaign is intensifying outreach to female voters and the Northeast, where he faces stronger resistance, shifting to a more moderate tone focused on cost of living, public safety, and household debt to broaden his base beyond traditional Bolsonarist strongholds.

item.title: Neymar na contagem regressiva: 10 jogos pelo Santos para convencer Ancelotti
item.description: Neymar has ten matches with Santos to convince Carlo Ancelotti to include him in Brazil’s final squad for the 2026 World Cup. The first opportunity comes this Tuesday (14) against Recoleta of Paraguay in the Copa Sudamericana.

item.title: FGTS para quitar dívidas: o que se sabe sobre a medida do governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government is studying the release of up to R$17 billion from the FGTS to help workers pay off debts, with R$9-10 billion for those earning up to five minimum wages (up to 20% of balance) and R$7 billion for 10 million workers in the anniversary withdrawal scheme who were fired without cause. The goal is to reduce household indebtedness, replace high-cost debt with cheaper funding, and stimulate consumption, pending a Provisional Measure.

item.title: Zema afirma que PL tem “frutas podres” e se diz “mais à direita”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for president, stated he considers himself 'more to the right' and criticized the PL for having 'rotten fruits,' indicating internal problems in the party. He said Novo applies stricter criteria, expelling those not aligned with its principles, and positioned himself as a right-wing figure who supports privatization, respects the Constitution, and opposes corruption. Despite his criticism, he acknowledged ongoing alliances with the PL in states such as Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, and Paraná.

item.title: Waller deixa o INSS com 2,7 milhões de pessoas na fila de espera
item.description: Gilberto Waller left the presidency of INSS with 2.7 million benefit requests awaiting analysis, following months of pressure to reduce the waiting queue. Despite a recent slight reduction, the backlog still exceeds the legal 45-day analysis deadline. New president Ana Cristina Viana Silveira takes on the challenge of speeding up benefit approvals in an election year, where the queue size will be a key campaign point for Lula’s government.

item.title: TSE deve eleger Nunes Marques presidente da Corte nesta semana
item.description: The TSE will elect Minister Nunes Marques as its new president on Tuesday for a two-year term, with André Mendonça as vice president. The selection will follow seniority order among the STF justices on the court, via secret ballot. Nunes Marques served as vice-president under Carmen Lúcia, who stepped down early to ensure a smooth transition.

item.title: Viagem de Lula à Europa terá 15 ministros e agendas com o empresariado
item.description: President Lula will travel to Europe from April 17 to 21, visiting Barcelona, Hannover, and Lisbon, accompanied by at least 15 ministers and heads of public agencies. The agenda includes signing bilateral agreements and meetings with over 100 private sector representatives, focusing on economic, technological, and environmental cooperation. The trip underscores the government’s strategy to attract investment and strengthen international partnerships in areas such as energy, industry, environment, and innovation.

item.title: Preso pelo ICE, Ramagem pode ser extraditado? Entenda
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem was arrested by ICE in the U.S. for being in irregular migratory status, after entering the country clandestinely in September 2025 to avoid trial in Brazil’s STF over alleged coup attempt. The Brazilian Justice Ministry had already formally requested his extradition in January 2026, and his ICE detention may now serve as the legal basis for removal and handover to Brazilian authorities.

item.title: Thiago Gagliasso detona o irmão, Bruno Gagliasso: ‘Vira homem’
item.description: Thiago Gagliasso, a Rio de Janeiro state deputy, publicly criticized his brother, actor Bruno Gagliasso, after Bruno met with President Lula and First Lady Janja da Silva in Brasília. Thiago accused Bruno of posing for a photo with Lula despite his criticisms of the government, suggested Bruno complained to their mother, and challenged him to 'be a man,' sparking backlash online, although many defended Bruno.

item.title: PF convida amiga de Lulinha para depor sobre fraudes no INSS
item.description: The Federal Police invited businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Lulinha (President Lula's son), to testify regarding billion-dollar frauds in the INSS under Operation Sem Desconto. She received R$1.5 million from Antonio Camilo Antunes, suspected of leading the scheme, and is alleged to have acted as an intermediary between him and Lulinha. Her defense states she already provided detailed written explanations and is available for further testimony, denying any wrongdoing.

item.title: Como a direita bolsonarista reagiu à prisão de Alexandre Ramagem nos EUA
item.description: Allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro are contesting the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem in the United States, claiming he is legally present under a pending political asylum request and that his detention was merely due to a minor traffic violation. The Brazilian government confirmed the arrest as part of a cooperation agreement with the U.S., citing an outstanding arrest warrant against Ramagem for attempted coup d'état. Bolsonarist influencers Paulo Figueiredo and Sóstenes Cavalcante deny any connection to the STF's extradition request and assert that Brazil had no involvement in the action.

item.title: Lula intensifica imagem de ‘rato de academia’ em busca do quarto mandato, diz ‘The Guardian’
item.description: Lula is intensifying his 2026 re-election campaign by sharing videos of his gym routine to project an image of physical vitality and readiness for a fourth term despite being 80 years old. The strategy, highlighted by The Guardian, aims to contrast his fitness with that of his 44-year-old rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, who fainted during a televised debate in 2016. The videos, frequently posted by allies and First Lady Janja, are well-received by supporters and reinforce the narrative that Lula remains capable of leading Brazil until 2030.

item.title: Foragido no Brasil, Ramagem é preso nos Estados Unidos pelo Serviço de Imigração
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former federal deputy and ex-director of Brazil's intelligence agency (Abin), was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after being a fugitive from Brazil since September 2025. He was sentenced by the STF to 16 years and one month in prison for attempting a coup d'état, violently abolishing the democratic state, and participating in a criminal organization. Ramagem fled using a diplomatic passport after illegally crossing into Guyana, despite having his regular passport seized and being barred from leaving the country by court order.

item.title: Meses antes de ser preso, Ramagem disse estar ‘seguro’ nos EUA
item.description: Months before being arrested by ICE in Orlando, former deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) claimed he was 'safe' in the United States, alleging U.S. government approval and denouncing STF rulings as illegal. He had been sentenced to 16 years in prison for his role in the coup attempt, though appeals were still pending. His escape was uncovered after he was spotted at a luxury Miami hotel in November 2025, and Brazilian authorities had already requested his extradition in December 2025.

item.title: ‘Ao menos estamos livres’, disse Eduardo Bolsonaro em foto ao lado de Ramagem nos EUA em fevereiro
item.description: In February, Eduardo Bolsonaro posted a photo with Alexandre Ramagem and Allan do Santos in the U.S., claiming they were 'free' despite being unable to return to Brazil and vowing to continue fighting for liberty. Ramagem was arrested by ICE on March 13 after fleeing Brazil via Roraima and Guyana, having been sentenced to 16 years for his role in the STF’s coup plot trial. The post emphasizes the alleged persecution of Bolsonaro allies, including frozen bank accounts and employment bans.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula assina decreto sobre reembolso-creche
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a decree regulating childcare reimbursement and expanding the 40-hour weekly workday for outsourced workers in the federal public administration. The ceremony, attended by Ministers Esther Dweck, Luiz Marinho, and Guilherme Boulos, included a review of measures implemented since 2023, such as hiring by category wage floor, year-end recess rights, vacation organization, and reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours in 12 service categories.

item.title: Negar candidatura de Lula é como duvidar que o homem foi à Lua
item.description: Lula da Silva showed ambiguity about his 2026 candidacy, saying he hasn’t decided yet but that it’s hard to imagine him not running. This stance is seen as a political strategy to maintain control over the PT and attract attention, similar to past instances where he tested party loyalty before consolidating as the sole candidate. Doubting his candidacy is likened to moon landing denial — reflecting wishful thinking rather than realistic analysis.

item.title: Sancionada lei que cria a Semana Nacional do Esporte
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.386/2026, establishing the National Sports Week, to be celebrated annually during the week of June 23. The law amends Article 207 of Law 14.597/2023, extending the National Sports Day observance to a full week, with activities led by public authorities in collaboration with schools, sports organizations, and civil society. The goal is to promote sports practice to enhance health, social inclusion, education, and quality of life.

item.title: Milícia de Trump deu a Ramagem o autoritarismo que ele queria por aqui
item.description: The arrest of Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's Intelligence Agency (ABIN) and a federal deputy aligned with Bolsonarismo, was carried out by ICE, the U.S. immigration agency known for controversial operations under the Trump administration. The event is framed as an authoritarian parallel between Ramagem's actions in Brazil and Trump's repressive policies toward migrants. The headline suggests Ramagem sought to replicate in Brazil the authoritarian model he admired in Trump.

item.title: Lula vai defender democracia e comércio em giro por países europeus que mais apoiaram acordo Mercosul-UE
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva begins a nearly week-long trip to Europe to defend democracy, multilateralism, and the Mercosul-EU agreement, meeting with leaders from countries that most supported the treaty. The agenda includes discussions on international trade and global cooperation amid current challenges.

item.title: Ex-diretor da Abin Alexandre Ramagem é preso pelo ICE nos EUA, diz mídia
item.description: Former Brazilian Intelligence Agency (Abin) director Alexandre Ramagem was arrested by ICE in the United States after fleeing Brazil in September, according to Brazilian media citing the Federal Police. His arrest follows his conviction in connection with an attempted coup involving former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Nome de Ramagem aparece em site do ICE: 'Sob custódia'
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem, sentenced by Brazil's Supreme Court to 16 years in prison for attempting a coup, was arrested by ICE in Orlando, Florida, after fleeing Brazil in September 2025. He is currently in ICE custody on immigration violations, with Brazilian authorities notified by the Federal Police, awaiting a decision on his extradition or return to Brazil.

item.title: O recálculo político de Alexandre Silveira
item.description: Minister Alexandre Silveira’s Senate candidacy plans in Minas Gerais have collapsed due to lack of political space after the party window, with President Lula deciding he will remain in office. Silveira now signals dual support for Lula’s re-election and Mateus Simões’ gubernatorial bid, maintaining good relations with the former Zema vice-governor, while his relationship with Rodrigo Pacheco remains strained. Despite lacking a viable party to run under, he attempts to mobilize the pro-government base in Minas, though much of it has shifted to other parties and the trend favors the PSD.

item.title: Alexandre Ramagem é preso nos EUA, diz PF; o que se sabe
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL) was arrested in the United States, where he had been a fugitive since September 2025 after being sentenced to 16 years in prison by the STF for his role in the January 8 coup attempt. The arrest was confirmed by the Brazilian Federal Police. Ramagem had fled Brazil clandestinely via the Guyana border, using a diplomatic passport, and his mandate was revoked in December 2025.

item.title: Caiado renunciou ao governo de Goiás, mas deixou ao menos seis parentes em cargos comissionados
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado resigned as governor of Goiás in March, but at least six of his relatives remain in appointed positions within the state government, including Adriano da Rocha Lima, who earned above the constitutional ceiling last month. These relatives hold various roles across state agencies, with salaries reaching up to 29,7 thousand reais, and Caiado is attempting to position his wife, Gracinha, as a Senate candidate. While the hiring of cousins is not legally classified as nepotism in Brazil — as they are considered fourth-degree relatives — the situation raises ethical concerns about the use of public office for familial benefit.

item.title: Alckmin minimiza impacto e diz que pesquisa é “momento”
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin downplayed the impact of recent electoral polls, stating they reflect only the current situation and that the true electoral landscape will be defined only after party conventions. He emphasized that the effective campaign begins only after conventions, when candidates are officially known and comparable. The Datafolha poll showed Lula tied with Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema in second-round scenarios.

item.title: TSE define novo comando nesta semana após saída antecipada de Cármen Lúcia
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will define its new leadership next Tuesday, the 14th, following the early departure of Minister Carmen Lucía. Kassio Nunes Marques will be appointed president and André Mendonça vice-president, marking the first time two Bolsonaro-appointed STF ministers simultaneously hold the TSE’s top two positions. The early transition aims to ensure stability and a smooth handover ahead of the 2026 elections, with a focus on depolarization, electronic voting transparency, and reinforcing the Court’s political neutrality.

item.title: Quem é Alexandre Ramagem, ex-deputado condenado pelo STF por tentativa de golpe que foi detido pelo ICE nos EUA
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former federal deputy of PL-RJ and former head of Abin, was detained by ICE in Orlando, Florida, over immigration issues while walking on the street. He was convicted by the STF in 2025 to 16 years and one month in prison for attempted coup, had his mandate revoked in December 2025, and ran for mayor of Rio in 2024, finishing in second place.

item.title: Ramagem foi abordado na rua pelo ICE em Orlando, teve documentos analisados e acabou preso
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former federal deputy of the PL party, was arrested in Orlando, USA, by ICE after being approached on the street and having his documents checked. He has been a fugitive since leaving Brazil clandestinely in 2025 to avoid serving a 16-year prison sentence imposed by the STF for attempted coup d'état. Brazil had already formally requested his extradition to the U.S. in December 2025, and his arrest was enabled by his inclusion in Interpol's list, as ordered by Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Rejeição a PT e dívidas: a estratégia de Flávio Bolsonaro por apoio do agro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) aims to retain agribusiness voter support by fostering rejection of the PT among rural producers and emphasizing the debts they accumulated during Lula’s government, according to sources in his pre-campaign speaking to UOL.

item.title: "Presidente do INSS foi sacrificado para conter dano", diz líder do PL
item.description: PL chamber leader Sóstenes Cavalcante accused the government of firing INSS president Gilberto Waller as a 'damage containment' move following revelations in the INSS CPMI. He claimed the dismissal was not coincidental and that someone is always 'sacrificed' when pressure mounts and truth emerges. Waller served 11 months before being replaced by career civil servant Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, amid a record backlog of 3.1 million benefit requests in February 2026.

item.title: Ex-major preso pede para sair de presídio por ter “eleitores” de Lula. Veja vídeo
item.description: Former Major Ailton Gonçalves Moraes Barros, arrested by the PF under Minister Alexandre de Moraes' order, requested release from Benfica prison (RJ) citing life risk due to the presence of 'Lula voters' among inmates. He argued his ex-military status is less relevant to his safety than political factors, and requested transfer to Bangu 8. The arrest is part of the coup plot investigation by the STF.

item.title: Governo diz que fila do INSS recuou em março, mas que está no mesmo tamanho de um ano atrás
item.description: In March 2026, the INSS backlog for benefits such as pensions and BPC decreased from 3.1 million to 2.7 million, with a record 1.625 million cases processed, yet remained at the same level as March 2025 due to a daily influx of 61,000 new applications. On the same day, President Gilberto Waller was dismissed and replaced by career servant Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, a move attributed to President Lula aiming to reduce political damage ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reforça negociações por aliança; PP e União Brasil sinalizam apoio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) intensified negotiations to form an electoral alliance with the centrão and is close to securing support from the União Progressista federation, composed of União Brasil and PP. The move aims to strengthen his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy.
